Salmon River is a rural neighbourhood in the Township of Langley, named for the Salmon River that crosses its northern side; in the Township's Official Community Plan (OCP) the planned community here is called the Salmon River Uplands, designated in the Township's Rural Plan.

The working street grid is 240 Street running north–south, with 48 Avenue, 52 Avenue, 56 Avenue and Fraser Highway crossing east–west; the Fraser Highway Employment Lands plan area beside it runs along Fraser Highway roughly from 228 Street to 240 Street, bounded by 48 Avenue to the north and Old Yale Road and 40 Avenue to the south.

The stock is single-family houses on large rural lots: the Township's council reports describe the existing pattern in the uplands as Suburban Residential Zone SR-1 lots of roughly 0.38 to 0.81 hectares (about 0.93 to 2.0 acres) along 240 Street, 248 Street and the avenues.

The Salmon River Uplands Engineering Servicing Plan (2024) plans municipal water and sanitary sewer extensions for the area — many existing homes predate those services, so servicing varies lot by lot.

blocks.text: Salmon River: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The Rural Plan policy for the Salmon River Uplands is one sentence long in effect: the Township's report quotes it as the area "shall be maintained for rural residential and agricultural uses" — there is no urban neighbourhood plan promising higher density here.

Minimum lot sizes are set by zone: Rural Zone RU-1 requires 1.7 hectares (4.2 acres) for a new lot, and Suburban Residential SR-1 requires 3,716 square metres (0.91 acres), per the Township Zoning Bylaw 1987 No. 2500 figures quoted in council reports.

ALR land cannot be excluded or subdivided for housing without the Agricultural Land Commission (ALC): in 2018 Township Council refused to even refer an exclusion application for 5990 – 240 Street and the 6000 block of 240 Street to the ALC, because it conflicted with the OCP, the Rural Plan and the regional growth strategy.

The Salmon River itself is protected where it crosses a development site: the Township requires the river corridor to be dedicated and protected as a non-disturbance Streamside Protection and Enhancement Area (SPEA) under Schedule 3 of the Langley OCP.

Hatchery Creek (the Nicomekl River headwaters, also called Hatchery Creek in Township studies) is a Class A watercourse, and subdivision layouts near it must respect top-of-bank setbacks confirmed by a qualified professional.

blocks.text: Salmon River: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Community amenity contributions are negotiated subdivision by subdivision in the uplands: the Township's December 2025 report records $7,500,000 in contributions for the 56-lot project at 5759 – 240 Street under the previous policy (about $133,929 per lot), and $125,000 for the single added lot at 25027 – 52 Avenue — there is no single standard charge a buyer can assume across the area.

The 56-lot subdivision at 5759 – 240 Street was required to keep 22.3% of its developable area as open space and a 15-metre treed greenspace buffer after a July 2023 Council resolution cut its lot count — the look of the new streets here is set by that negotiation, lot by lot.

Water quality and capacity in the area's five aquifers are named in the Township's Fraser Highway Employment Lands plan as primary concerns — a well-served lot here needs its water source checked, not assumed.

Hatchery Creek supports salmonid species and Best Creek (also called Trigg Creek) supports coho salmon and trout, so creek-side lots carry streamside setbacks that can shrink the buildable area well inside the lot lines.

blocks.text: Salmon River: development and new projects

items.t: 23700 block of 56 Avenue — Salmon River Uplands; applicant Infinity Properties Ltd.; rezoning application No. 100637 (Township of Langley Zoning Bylaw 1987 No. 2500 Amendment Bylaw No. 5782) to rezone part of a 43.6-hectare (107.8-acre) site to Suburban Residential SR-3 for 58 single-family lots. Status: staff report to Council December 15, 2025 recommending first, second and third reading subject to 10 development prerequisites before final reading (as of November 3, 2026).

5759 – 240 Street — Salmon River Uplands; 56 single-family lots (Township Project No. 11-09-0033). Status: granted third reading November 20, 2023, as reported in the Township's December 2025 council report (as of November 3, 2026).
25027 – 52 Avenue — Salmon River Uplands; two-lot subdivision (Township Project No. 11-02-0071). Status: granted third reading December 1, 2025 (as of November 3, 2026).

Fraser Highway Employment Lands Reference Plan — along Fraser Highway from about 228 Street to 240 Street, adjacent to Salmon River Uplands; Township of Langley plan for employment uses on about 152 hectares, with no ALR land inside the plan area. Status: reference plan published by the Township (as of November 3, 2026).

The Township of Langley's total 2025 residential tax rate was 3.34910 per $1,000 of assessed value, of which the total municipal rate under Bylaw 6128 was 1.87580 per $1,000 — the Township's own 2025 Property Tax Rates table.

Township utility charges (water, sewer, solid waste) are billed separately from the tax notice — the Township began mailing utility fees on a separate statement in 2025 — and the tax due date is July 2, with a 5% penalty on current-year taxes unpaid after that date.
The Speculation and Vacancy Tax (SVT) applies: the Township of Langley is a Metro Vancouver municipality on the Province's taxable-areas list.

No TransLink fixed-route bus was found serving the Salmon River Uplands streets (240 Street, 48–56 Avenues) in the operator material read; the nearest transit exchanges are in Langley Centre and Aldergrove.
School transport is by SD35 bus or car for most uplands addresses, since no school sits inside the neighbourhood.

blocks.text: Salmon River: risks and due diligence

items.t: Creek setbacks are the lot-level risk: the Salmon River must be dedicated as a non-disturbance Streamside Protection and Enhancement Area where it crosses a site, and Hatchery Creek is a Class A watercourse with top-of-bank setbacks — check the Township's streamside mapping (OCP Schedule 3) for the specific lot.

Check ALR status on the Agricultural Land Commission's mapping before assuming a second dwelling, subdivision or non-farm business: Council's 2018 refusal to refer the 240 Street exclusion application shows exclusion is not a formality here.

Servicing is the third check: confirm whether the lot is on municipal water and sewer under the Salmon River Uplands Engineering Servicing Plan (2024) or on a private well and septic, and whether connection charges apply.

What the Township pages do not tell a buyer: the yield or water quality of an individual well, or a septic system's condition — those need the well log, Fraser Health records and an inspection, not the plan documents.

faq.q: Is Salmon River in the Agricultural Land Reserve?
faq.a: Partly — and the line runs through the neighbourhood, not around it. Township reports describe ALR parcels on 240 Street inside the Salmon River Uplands designation, while other uplands lots are zoned SR-1 and SR-3 suburban residential outside the ALR. Check the specific parcel on the ALC's mapping and the Township's zoning, because ALR status decides whether subdivision or a non-farm use is even possible.

faq.q: How big are the lots, and can they be split?
faq.a: Existing SR-1 lots run about 0.38 to 0.81 hectares, the RU-1 rural zone sets a 1.7-hectare minimum for new lots, and new subdivisions here are being approved at SR-3 density only through rezoning — a 58-lot proposal at the 23700 block of 56 Avenue went to Council in December 2025. Splitting an existing acreage is a rezoning or ALC question, not a right.

faq.q: Is there municipal water and sewer, or well and septic?
faq.a: It depends on the street. The Township's Salmon River Uplands Engineering Servicing Plan (2024) plans municipal water and sanitary sewer for the area, and recent subdivision approvals have required sewerage service as a condition — older homes away from the new mains may still be on well and septic, so verify the specific lot's services with the Township.

Langley School District (SD35) assigns by street address and tells families to use its online School Locator for the catchment school; there is no school inside the Salmon River Uplands itself, so children are bused or driven to schools in the surrounding Murrayville, Otter and Aldergrove areas — confirm the exact schools for the address before subjects.

faq.q: Is the Salmon River district in a floodplain?
faq.a: The valley is Fraser River floodplain land; the Township states the Salmon River Pump Station provides flood protection when Fraser River levels rise and was built to mitigate flooding of the surrounding agricultural lands during freshet.

faq.q: Which schools serve a Salmon River address?
faq.a: For the sample address 4452 256 Street, the SD35 School Locator returns North Otter Elementary and D.W. Poppy Secondary, with no middle school shown; other addresses may fall in different catchments. Coghlan Fundamental Elementary at 4452 256 Street is a district choice school on the upland east side.

faq.q: Is the land in the ALR?
faq.a: Farm land in the valley is in the Agricultural Land Reserve in places; confirm a specific parcel on the ALC ALR maps.
